Hi Alex — thanks for the note and the timeline. We can absolutely provide an evidence packet. High level before I send the package:

- Redwood reports p50/p95 over rolling 30-day windows by default, with regional aggregation. Measurement excludes SRs where a higher-tier fallback (regional fallback, model variant) was in effect.
- Sampling: we compute percentiles over full request population (no downsampling) for hosted customers. We apply a transient noise carveout for detectable upstream network blackouts (documented).
- For ramp periods we can offer a 6-week temporary measurement grace that excludes the first 48 hours after any major deployment change and allows a "ramp carveout" for obvious seasonal spikes. This would be written into the SLO amendment.

I'll attach our evidence export for the last 30 days and a short explainer from Engineering. Markus (cc'd) is adding a time-series CSV and a short note on statistical methods. > A few clarifications inline:
>
> 1) Rolling windows vs fixed buckets: we compute rolling 30-day percentiles (not calendar-month buckets) to avoid boundary effects during cutovers. That means any day the customer asks, the p50/p95 reflect the prior 30 days ending at that timestamp.
>
> 2) Outlier handling: we do NOT truncate the distribution; instead we annotate requests that match upstream network errors and place them into a separate telemetry channel excluded from SLO computation. We include both raw and filtered counts in the evidence zip so auditors can reproduce our exclusion logic.
>
> 3) Daypart normalization: for customers with very spiky traffic (e.g., nightly batch spikes) we offer an optional daypart-adjusted SLO which computes percentiles per-hour-of-day then aggregates to reduce the impact of predictable bursts. This is an opt-in feature and would be added to the agreement.
>
> 4) Ramp carveout proposal: for your ramp period we propose a 6-week "soft measurement" where deviations that are limited to the first 48 hours after any major model or config change are excluded. We also allow a single 72-hour carveout window for migration days.
>
> 5) Evidence provenance: all artifacts are signed and include telemetry checksums; we can provide an auditor account with view-only access to the raw traces on request.
>
